note: Currulao is both the marimba dance gathering and a family of genres played at it (bambuco viejo, pango, juga, bunde, berejú), so many tracks are jugas or bundes rather than a song called currulao. Colombian groups from Guapi and Timbiquí lead here, with Papá Roncón for the Ecuadorian side in Esmeraldas.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Known releases are small-label and festival-driven: Smithsonian Folkways (Grupo Naidy, 2005, 12 tracks; the group had two earlier CDs), Canalón de Timbiquí (four albums 2004–2019), Grupo Bahía/Hugo Candelario, Herencia de Timbiquí (four albums 2006–2014, fusion), Ecuadorian Esmeraldas marimba (Papá Roncón and others), plus the annual Petronio Álvarez festival in Cali (since 1996, with a marimba category) whose groups often self-release. Commercial recording seems to start in the 1970s (Pascual de Andagoya). Perhaps 100–300 albums of 10–14 tracks, many fusion; an insider's essential list is about 40 performances.
